nodes.text: Let $f:\mathbb{N}\to \mathbb{R}$ be an additive function (i.e. $f(ab)=f(a)+f(b)$ whenever $(a,b)=1$). If there is a constant $c$ such that $\lvert f(n+1)-f(n)\rvert <c$ for all $n$ then must there exist some $c'$ such that\[f(n)=c'\log n+O(1)?\]

#491 : [Er61,p.237] [Er72,p.85] [Er82e,p.65] number theory Erdős [Er46] proved that if $f(n+1)-f(n)=o(1)$ or $f(n+1)\geq f(n)$ then $f(n)=c\log n$ for some constant $c$. This is true, and was proved by Wirsing [Wi70] . See also [897] and [1122] .
